gen-fs-nippo-gf-stack-sans-text: Wiry, technical, a bit cheeky. Stack Sans Text takes the opposite job from Nippo: where the heading shows off its proud small letters, this plain sans keeps a marker-like line and generous lowercase for the reading.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-vend-sans: Nippo stands out with small letters nearly as big as its capitals, cut like bent wire. Vend Sans sits beneath it in a ruler-straight line with wide open curve endings, filling each line with lowercase that feels generous.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-yaldevi: Bent rope, bent tubing: that is the Nippo heading, with lines that curl and bounce. Yaldevi handles the quieter work, with an e that opens clearly to the right and oversized lowercase proportions in plain sans-serif.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-hind-siliguri: Hind Siliguri hums along in a flat gray texture, its rounds cracked open like a bangle and capitals rising only slightly above the lowercase. Oswald packs its rows tightly above it.
gen-fs-panchang-clash-grotesk: Clash Grotesk keeps every stroke uniform in a plain sans line. Panchang is the one to look at, with spacious gaps between each stem and curve and a read that never snags on a closed bowl.
gen-fs-panchang-fs-merriweather-sans: Merriweather Sans reads sturdy and large, its lowercase making words feel substantial and its e opening clearly to the right. And Panchang answers with strokes carrying the same visual weight throughout, which is exactly where the pair connects.
gen-fs-panchang-general-sans: Confident from the first line, Panchang draws its strokes like a pulled string and leaves open space around every stem and curve. And General Sans follows with a steady pen pressure and lowercase that fills the line, moving smoothly around each bend.
gen-fs-panchang-gf-science-gothic: Panchang never snags on a closed-up bowl, its strokes steady as a drawn string with open gaps between stem and curve. Science Gothic sets its stroke ends far apart, so reading a longer passage goes one letter at a time, unhurried and uniform.
gen-fs-panchang-gf-syncopate: Expressive and open, Panchang draws its strokes with drawn-string steadiness and leaves generous gaps around each curve. And Syncopate keeps that going in sans-serif, its open c, e and s shapes spaced like rungs on a rope ladder, steady as a technical pen.
gen-fs-panchang-switzer: Wire-like, open and sure of itself. Switzer brings tubular, wire-like letterforms and c tips that never creep toward touching, giving this pair its strongest quality: a clean, unsnagged read from Panchang down to the sans below.
